fullPassage:
One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.

Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our identity. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!

Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.

Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.

Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."

The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should assume that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.

Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.

In the Parana Delta near Buenos Aires, Argentina, is a small island called "The Eye," which floats in the middle of a small lake that is about 120 meters in diameter. It was accidentally discovered by Argentinian film director Sergio Neuspiller during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials. Interestingly, both the island and the lake are perfectly circular. What's more, the lake that surrounds the island is extremely cold and clear — an unusual phenomenon for the area. So mysterious is the island that people have wondered if it was created naturally or by aliens. Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.

② increasing: 화면이 파란 파장 노출량을 늘림 — 적절
③ suppresses: 파란빛이 멜라토닌 분비를 억제함 — 적절
④ weakens: 고글 없는 집단의 결과가 이론을 '약화'시킨다? 실험 결과는 파란빛이 수면을 해친다는 이론을 '뒷받침(supports)'하므로 반대 ←정답
det.tip: 실험 결과는 이론을 supports(뒷받침). weakens(약화)는 정반대

questions.passage: Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most (A)[relaxing / challenging] competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most (B)[easy / difficult], taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are (C)[provided / banned], so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) challenging=힘든 / relaxing=편안한 (B) difficult=어려운 / easy=쉬운 (C) provided=제공되는 / banned=금지된
det.analysis:
① challenging—difficult—provided: 늪·강·해변을 지나는 '힘든' 대회 + 6구간 경주가 가장 '어려운' + 기본 필수품만 '제공되는' 흐름 ←정답
② relaxing/banned: 편안한/금지된은 문맥과 반대
③ easy: 일주일 넘게 걸리는 경주가 '쉬운' 것은 모순
④ relaxing/easy/banned: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 늪·강을 지나고 필수품만 주어지는 → challenging(힘든)·difficult(어려운)·provided(제공되는)

questions.passage: Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was (A)[heated / cooled] to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was (B)[separated / combined] with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a (C)[different / similar] process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) heated=가열된 / cooled=식은 (B) combined=결합된 / separated=분리된 (C) similar=비슷한 / different=다른
det.analysis:
(A) 광물 스티브나이트를 승화시키려면 '가열(heated)'해야 해요. '식히면(cooled)' 기체가 안 생겨요.
(B) kohl에 al-을 '결합해(combined)' al-kohl을 만들었어요. '분리했다(separated)'는 반대예요.
(C) 증류는 승화와 '비슷한(similar)' 과정이라고 했어요. '다른(different)'은 문맥에 안 맞아요.
③ heated — combined — similar ←정답
det.tip: 가열(heated) → 결합(combined) → 비슷한(similar) 과정

questions.passage: The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should (A)[doubt / assume] that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can (B)[seek / avoid] being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely (C)[reject / accept] slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) assume=가정하다 / doubt=의심하다 (B) avoid=피하다 / seek=추구하다 (C) reject=거부하다 / accept=받아들이다
det.analysis:
① assume—avoid—reject: 어떤 위치든 될 수 있다고 '가정하고' + 편향을 '피하며' + 노예제를 '거부한다' ←정답
② doubt—avoid—reject: (A) 위치에 처할 수 있다고 '의심'이 아니라 '가정'해야 함
③ assume—seek—accept: (B) 편향을 '추구'하는 게 아니라 '피함', (C) 노예제를 '받아들임'이 아니라 '거부함'
④ doubt—seek—reject: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 어떤 위치든 될 수 있다 assume(가정) → 편향 avoid(피함) → 노예제 reject(거부)

questions.passage: Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it (A)[unafraid / afraid] of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great (B)[advantage / weakness] when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 (C)[dull / sharp] teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) unafraid=두려워하지 않는 / afraid=두려워하는 (B) advantage=이점, 유리함 / weakness=약점 (C) sharp=날카로운 / dull=무딘
det.analysis:
① afraid—advantage—sharp: (A) 뱀을 사냥하는 몽구스라 '두려워하지 않는(unafraid)'이 맞음
② unafraid—advantage—sharp: 뱀을 '두려워하지 않고(unafraid)' + 날렵한 몸이 '이점(advantage)'을 주고 + '날카로운(sharp)' 이빨 ←정답
③ unafraid—weakness—dull: (B)(C) 날렵함은 '이점(advantage)'이고 이빨은 '날카로움(sharp)'
④ afraid—advantage—dull: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: unafraid(두려워하지 않는) 몽구스, advantage(이점), sharp(날카로운) 이빨

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person who studies a subject carefully in order to discover new facts"

det.korean: tourist=관광객 / artist=예술가 / director=감독 / researcher=연구자
det.analysis:
① tourist: 관광객 — 새로운 사실을 연구하는 사람이 아님
② artist: 예술가 — 연구가 본업이 아님
③ director: 감독 — 영화 등을 지휘하는 사람
④ researcher: 새로운 사실을 발견하려 주제를 신중히 연구하는 사람 ←정답
det.tip: studies ... to discover new facts = 연구자(researcher)

questions.passage: One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps ①<u>process</u> sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and ②<u>objects</u> on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the ③<u>same</u> side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only ④<u>shave</u> the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① process=처리하다 ② objects=사물 ③ same→opposite (부적절) ④ shave=면도하다
det.analysis:
① process: 두정엽이 감각 정보를 '처리' — 적절
② objects: 사람, 소리, '사물'을 인지하지 못함 — 적절
③ same: '같은'(same) 쪽을 못 느낀다? 각 반구는 반대쪽을 통제하므로 손상의 '반대편'(opposite)을 못 느낌. same은 반대 ←정답
④ shave: 인지되는 왼쪽만 '면도' — 적절
det.tip: 각 반구는 반대쪽을 통제 → 손상의 '반대편'(opposite)을 못 느낌. same(같은)은 정반대

questions.passage: Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel ①<u>relaxed</u> when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is ②<u>perceived</u> as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher ③<u>pitch</u> than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our ④<u>identity</u>. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 ① relaxed가 문맥상 부적절 (원래 uncomfortable). ② perceived=인식되는 ③ pitch=음높이 ④ identity=정체성
det.analysis:
① relaxed: 녹음을 들을 때 '느긋함'? 글 전체가 창피·불편(uncomfortable)을 말하므로 반대 ←정답
② perceived: 뼈 전달음은 더 깊게 인식된다 — 적절
③ pitch: 목소리가 더 높은 음높이를 가진다 — 적절
④ identity: 목소리는 정체성의 중요한 일부 — 적절
det.tip: 녹음을 들으면 uncomfortable(불편)해함. relaxed(느긋한)는 글 전체 흐름과 반대

questions.passage: Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a __________ that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
